sources.cartographic_provenance: The original GIS chapter describes a new thematic composition using Landsat imagery, varied IGM and SEGEMAR base cartography, image interpretation and FUNDAL GPS fieldwork. sources.actual_material_read: Original 124-page PDF. Front matter and project description at printed pages 1 and 5; selected hydrological passages at 36, 38, 43–45, 77–78, 81 and 95; Map 1 at 36; annex map overview at 113–124; full-page and northeastern views of Caminos, ferrocarril y poblaciones en el ANP at 120 and Espejos y Cursos de aguas sobre curvas de nivel at 124. observations: Valcheta is named within the endorheic Curicó basin.
The plan identifies Brazo Frío and Brazo Caliente spring headwaters and their La Horqueta union.
The hydrological account separates plateau recharge, spring emergence, ephemeral streams and the more persistent Valcheta watercourse.
The plan states that Valcheta discharges to Curicó outside the protected area.
The actual original maps supply regional terrain, locality, valley and lake-setting correspondence, but insufficient detail for all selected through-links and the final endpoint.
sources.limits: Historical regional management cartography, not a present-flow observation or an official river-name registry. Pale generalized hydrography, small-scale labeling and unlabeled lake polygons leave material correspondence gaps. Protected-area boundaries and basin membership are not river continuity evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen desert opening and approach to the All-American Canal corridor
correspondence.finding: The chosen eastern opening is in the desert north of the All-American Canal and west of Felicity. The original distinguishes the canal, the Interstate 8 crossing, the dunes, and the Coachella Canal branch farther west. The selection approaches and briefly occupies the broad All-American Canal corridor but also crosses intervening desert/dune terrain. No mapped continuous watercourse connects the actual opening to the full chosen southwestward and then northwestward passage. This is not evidence that the selected opening is the source of the Alamo River or a continuous named canal.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestward East Mesa passage to East Highline Canal and the agricultural grid
correspondence.finding: The Coachella Canal is clearly mapped northeast of much of this long selected interval. The selection instead traverses the intervening East Mesa desert and the Holtville Carrier Landing Site / Inkey Barley Range setting before approaching the East Highline Canal at the agricultural boundary. The original shows the East Highline Canal and nearby Holtville drain/lateral network, but no continuous channel establishing this entire desert-to-grid transfer. Nearby canal labels do not supply the missing selected through-connection.

correspondence.component_scope: East-west Kendle Road agricultural waterway, Holtville Main Drain and Alamo River junction
correspondence.finding: The east-west selection follows the mapped agricultural-waterway alignment along Kendle/Adams Road toward Alamo River. The western portion is explicitly labeled Holtville Main Drain, and the source shows its junction with Alamo River. Near Gibbs Road a named north-south Holtville Main Drain section joins this alignment. The eastern selected continuation toward East Highline Canal is mapped in the managed grid but lacks an unambiguous repeated Holtville Main Drain label. The bounded name is therefore attached to the actually labeled western drain and its river junction, not asserted for every eastern lateral or the preceding desert passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected Alamo River reach east of Brawley and toward Calipatria
correspondence.finding: Repeated Alamo River labels and connected channel cartography support the selected northward river corridor east of Brawley and onward toward Calipatria. Numerous agricultural drains join it; the source distinguishes this river from the New River farther west. Gieselmann Lake, Wiest Lake, Finney Lake and Ramer Lake are distinguishable side-waterbody settings beside the mapped Alamo channel. Generalized selected segments clip some lake-edge settings, but the original does not justify treating all these lakes as a serial through-lake route. Vail Supply Canal, Rockwood Canal and the surrounding agricultural grid are separately labeled. The regional Water Board overview independently identifies Alamo River as receiving substantial Imperial Valley agricultural return flow and discharging to Salton Sea.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Alamo delta, managed pond grid and selected Salton Sea entry
correspondence.finding: The originals show lower Alamo River entering Salton Sea near the Red Hill Road / Red Island setting. The selected continuation trends more directly northwest through the adjacent mapped pond/drain mosaic before reaching the lake fill. This establishes the ordinary delta, managed-water and receiving-lake setting; it does not establish the specific selected through-connection across the pond-and-drain grid into the lake. Those distinctions are not used to invent a new river name or extend Alamo River across the entire lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Long northwestward Salton Sea interior continuation and actual ending
correspondence.finding: The remaining selected parts continue northwest through the cartographically labeled Salton Sea and end within the mapped lake interior. They do not terminate at the Alamo River mouth, leave the lake through an outlet, or become a natural river reach merely because the modeled object is a river group. Salton Sea is the supported terminal waterbody name; the cartography is not a present shoreline or lake-level survey.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern selected opening on the Somuncurá plateau
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies well within the plateau setting represented by the plan. The map shows terrain and scattered surface-water features, while the hydrology prose describes recharge through fractured basalt and spring emergence at the plateau margin. Neither the mapped faint linework nor that regional groundwater description establishes a surface-water through-course from this particular opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward upper approach from plateau toward the spring-fed corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected line follows a broadly northward upland-to-margin approach. The plan distinguishes spring-fed headwaters, temporary channels and plateau depressions, but does not visibly resolve this selected approach as a continuous tributary or identify its join to the named Valcheta source branches. No groundwater connection is substituted for a mapped surface link.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle northeastern valley and approach toward Valcheta
correspondence.finding: The original regional drainage map and annex place the selected corridor in the north-draining Valcheta-side valley network. Valcheta is an explicitly named watercourse in the plan, and its spring branches are described. The small-scale linework does not securely distinguish every chosen feeder and intermediate join, so regional alignment is retained without claiming complete selected-channel correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeast-running lower valley and Valcheta locality crossing
correspondence.finding: The selected line reaches the Valcheta locality/railway corridor shown on the independent management-plan mapping. The plan describes the Valcheta valley and hydrometric Dique I setting. This supports a regional Valcheta reach candidate but does not establish each selected channel, irrigation passage or join through the lower valley.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake/depression passage north of Valcheta
correspondence.finding: The original annex depicts a prominent lake cluster in the selected lower-corridor setting. The plan states that Valcheta drains to Curicó, outside the protected area. The grayscale map does not establish which individual lake polygon or shore-side passage corresponds to each selected part, or demonstrate a continuous selected exit from that lake setting.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern continuation and actual internal terminal
correspondence.finding: The preserved selected line continues north of the prominent mapped lake cluster, bends, and ends internally. The annex shows scattered smaller water/depression features in this area, but no sufficiently clear through-link or named receiving feature can be matched to the actual selected endpoint. The endpoint is not reassigned to Curicó merely because the source names the regional receiving basin.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northern opening
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is on the mountain-front apron between the separately mapped Sunnyside Creek and Idlewild Creek corridors. The original depicts those neighboring creeks but does not establish the selected westward opening or its southwestward transfer across the apron. Neither creek name is assigned to that selected opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern valley-axis continuation to the Cottonwood Creek setting
correspondence.finding: The selection follows the broad valley axis west of Ione, Berlin and Union, crossing the Sand Wash approach and continuing south. The map depicts separate ephemeral feeder channels, roads and the valley floor but does not establish a continuous selected through-connection to the southern wash. Valley membership, a road alignment and the neighboring stream labels do not close this gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Cottonwood Creek junction and upper mapped Ione Wash
correspondence.finding: At the Cottonwood Creek approach, the original shows a substantial sandy wash corridor continuing south along the western valley floor. Ione Wash is directly labelled farther south on that same corridor. This supports the selected corridor and the incoming Cottonwood Creek junction at ordinary geographic scale, without imposing the wash name on the unresolved northern opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern Ione Valley wetland, Golden Wash junction and Cloverdale Creek junction
correspondence.finding: The mapped wash continues southeast through an elongated marsh-symbol area, past the Golden Wash junction and through the narrowing valley into the lower sandy corridor. Cloverdale Creek approaches from the northeast and joins the selected receiving wash. The broad wash, wetland and connected valley passage support ordinary corridor correspondence; individual seasonal threads, present water conditions and precise junction vertices are not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Ione Wash beside the Peavine Creek wash system
correspondence.finding: Repeated Ione Wash labels occupy the broad southward sandy corridor followed by the selection. The cartography separately labels Peavine Creek in the eastern parallel wash complex. The selection is geographically supported through the lower Ione Wash corridor to its southern end north of US6. No single Peavine name is imported into the Ione opening, and the exact distribution of floodwater among parallel sandy threads is not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Departure from the mapped wash across US6 and the Millers plain
correspondence.finding: The selected route leaves the mapped sandy wash, crosses US6 west of Millers, passes west of the separately labelled Millers Pond, and runs southwest across the broad plain. The original depicts the plain and scattered ponds but no continuous selected channel or specified generalized wash-to-playa connection. The selection does not establish passage through Millers Pond merely because it passes nearby.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern playa passage and connection toward the final southern playa
correspondence.finding: The selected extension crosses an unnamed northern playa east of McLeans and then continues southwest over the intervening land toward a larger southern playa. Both playa outlines and the intervening ground are readable, but the map does not depict the selected through-connection between the two. These are separate mapped dry-lake/playa features; no common river or lake name is inferred from proximity.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected endpoint in the southern playa
correspondence.finding: The actual selected endpoint lies within the larger southern mapped playa southwest of McLeans, between the Monte Cristo Range and Lone Mountain surroundings. The original directly supports this terminal geographic setting. It supplies no displayed name for that playa and does not close the separately unresolved upstream inter-playa connection.

correspondence.component_scope: headward-opening
correspondence.finding: The regional location map covers the northern lake country but does not establish the chosen initial waterbody outlet or the selected first joins.

correspondence.component_scope: upper-westward-course
correspondence.finding: General lake-and-stream terrain is shown. The selected western bend and each intervening transfer cannot be followed securely at this overview scale.

correspondence.component_scope: middle-lake-approach
correspondence.finding: Armit Lake is labeled in the corresponding regional setting. Neither that label nor adjacent hydrography establishes every selected lake inlet, outlet and intervening transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: lower-course-and-terminal
correspondence.finding: Richard Lake and Robin Hood Bay are labeled in the lower regional setting. The selected final channel and its actual receiving-water connection remain unresolved.
